verdict.for_whom: Buy this if you want a massive adventure with rich choice and consequence and do not mind a steep learning curve or clunky camera controls, but skip it if you prefer fast-paced action and endless character leveling.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that movement feels janky, slow, or clunky, though some mention getting used to it.

citations.review_text:
This game is terrible. I wanted to love it like everyone else in the reviews. Went into it excited and I really tried. However, even after just 9-10 hours, I cannot for the life of me understand the praise. This game is so bad. The graphics and sound are alright, nothing near what some of these reviews would have you believe though. It's the gameplay and story that really stink it up here. I can't stress this enough: It's not as good as everyone makes it out to be, it's mid - at best. 

The movement is slow and kind of janky. The world is sort of.. restrictive. It doesn't feel very open. Stay on the main paths, wait for underwhelming encounters, then spend more time in dialogue and rolling the 20-sided die than you do in combat. It's just not fun. I felt no or very little sense of character progression during the time I played. The way abilities work is really dumb. I get they want you to make choices that matter as battles play out, but it's really a drag.

The story, once again, is not what all the praise would have you believe. I found myself not really giving a dook about the characters or choices I made. Who are the Squidward people? Where do they come from?  Why are they here? Honestly, I wanted to get into it, but I just didn't care no matter how much I tried. I mean, anytime I found myself the slightest bit immersed I was brought back to reality by the lousy camera and movement. 

Honestly, the whole experience feels cheap. For all the praise, this really is one big steaming pile of crap. All I hear though is Larian this, Larian that. "IsH gAm diS uH mAStuRpeeS" blah, blah, blah. I'm just glad I bought it on sale. If your not a fan boy super-mega-nerd, stay away and save your money. I've played turn based games before and enjoyed them well enough. This one though, is boooooaaaarrrrriiiiiinnnnnngggggggg...
great game so far ./.....movement is a little iffy but once you get use to it its all good
Really wanted to like it, but I absolutely hate the combat system, and I found the controls to be very clunky and unintuitive. Seems like it would be a great and immersive experience otherwise.

Fun for the right person!! 

Yeah it's a good game...but honestly...overhyped...it's fun it's got amazing D&D mechanics and story telling and choose your own way very D&D forsure...but what is this movement? What modern game doesn't let you use WASD for movement...it makes the whole game feel off and way less immersive....and why does my character never talk...just lips totally sealed shut during every cutscene and conversation...but i chose a voice for him to go 'ugh' and other minor combat noises? Also makes the game feel less immersive. The game as a whole is great but has a very...weird off feeling about it all... And I also think it's ridiculous one person can run off and basicslly do the whole story without you even knowing...no notification or nothing...that's a bit frustrating. Definitely glad I waited for it to be on a GOOD sale for once to get because if I paid full price I probabaly would of returned it. Kind of having a hard time getting into it for some reason.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs smoothly and performs well on PC and handheld devices.

citations.review_text: Runs very smoothly, and a lot of depth to the game

Come on, everyone loves this game.  I was just mostly waiting to be able to play it, then I saw that it would run on my Apple Silicon MacBookAir, and was on sale.  Definitely a bit much for GPUs on this little laptop, but functionally it runs pretty smoothly for the most part.  Definitely one of the better games of this type that I have played.  Easier to get rolling with than Divinity 2, and so far is  more narratively engaging than Pillars of Eternity.  I would definitely recommend it, but millions of others have already done so.  If you've got the itch, and especially if it's on sale, go ahead and buy it. You know you want to.

Bought this game a while back when it first released for Xbox and Bought it again recently on PC. Absolutely loving this game since wife and I are able to play together now. Graphics are absolutely stunning and the story of the game just keeps pulling me in more and more. so far we've just hit act 3 after I'd say about a month of play just from the content alone and exploring and getting into encounters. Can have some issues with the Larian servers but it's minor considering that's a 1st world issue. Along with that the Mod availability is amazing. currently with max setting pulling a solid consistent 144FPS matched to my monitor's Refresh rate.

eeeeeeh, guess its fine. not a high enough level or understand the game enough to really think its inncredible yet..... 6 hours in

Performance to Quality is GREAT!!!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that turn-based battles are slow and can last a long time.

citations.review_text:
This was praised extremely high, but i could not get over the boring hour-long turn-based battles.

Even compared to jrpgs, this is its own category of "falling asleep" battle system (i have the same problem with DND, where you roll 30 times to defeat a zubat.)
I thought it can't be too bad and the character customization and story writing makes up for it. But battles can take 1-2 hours or more.

So for me it was not a good entry into this genre of games, i spent too much time in the character creator and the first dungeon though to refund it. But do not sense a need to try it again anytime.

I don't like how much hype this game gets when it is incredibly confusing for a non-D&D player. I thought the game would properly show me the ropes, but I just end up confused even after the tutorial and first fights. The combat feels very slow on top of it, it's just not for me.

If you've never played D&D and know absolutely NOTHING about it, do NOT play this game.
Idk. There is a lot about this game I don't like. Story, Characters, difficulty, and writing. Hell, even the narrator is annoying. Combat is slow. Just not a fun experience.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: As players get deeper into the experience, those unfamiliar with the rules note a steep learning curve for the turn-based combat, though they recommend the game regardless. Camera navigation, particularly on vertical maps, continues to draw complaints, and there are reports of bugs like missing textures or loading issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the turn-based combat system has a steep learning curve and feels clunky or difficult to get used to initially for players unfamiliar with tactical or D&D-style rules.

citations.review_text: 40 hours in. Had to make myself stop playing the other night . Good game. Combat took some getting used to. Plenty of turn based game experience but not tactical turn base or whatever you'd call the BG3 combat system, so it was a bit clunky at first but got into it the more I played. Greatest game I've ever played after a few gummies.

Wonderful game! Great music, fun gameplay, interesting & entertaining story, freedom of choice, many different build options/approaches, popping HDR, great voice acting, etc. It is a bit difficult to learn at first if you've never even played so much as D&D or any turn-based game, but the effort and struggle is rewarding & worthwhile.

As someone coming into this game with very little knowledge about DnD and CRPGs, I had very high expecations based on the amount of people praising it online, calling it the "greatest RPG ever made", and all the awards and accolades it has received since its release in 2023. After playing the game for 75 hours, Baldur's Gate 3 is a step above in quality compared to other RPGs. The voice acting, character design, game mechanics and the narrative are all incredible. The amount of dialogue options and the myriad ways to complete the game is mind-blowing. The turn-based combat took me a lot of time to get used to but forces you to come up with a viable strategy in big fights (like in moonrise towers or the house of hope). 

This game is amazing but not for everyone. For those who like lengthy narratives and a traditional "choose your own adventure" game, then this game is for you. For those who play games for the gameplay or combat system (like souls games or FPS games), then I would not recommend this game. I had a blast playing through this game and will likely replay it again in the future.
It's a good game. I bit difficult for newcomers but all in all a true RP with a ton of depth and content.
Great game, a bit of a learning curve for someone not used to a game like this. However, even so, a ton of fun, can't stop playing.
It's slow and a lot to learn at first, especially if you've never played a crpg. I looked up tips and helpful channels on YouTube. Once it gets going, it's very good though.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the camera controls as frustrating and difficult to use, particularly when navigating vertical map environments.

citations.review_text: Not very fun to play. Camera angles are hard to use. Story is not drawing me in. For dnd feels like little to no player agency

Excellent story driven gameplay that makes each play through special I still haven't seen the end of act 2 as I like to collect everything I can but the support of multiplayer has made the game stand out by playing with friends. Negatives- Camera can be frustrating at times and if you leave a member behind the easiest way is to meet them at camp so it makes sending a character solo for errands a bit annoying that you can't warp to team mates out of combat. Highly recommend

I can't help but feel people have been glazing this game way too heavily. The story, characters, and very impressive accounting for different gameplay styles are intriguing- probably one of the best in recent years. It actually reminds me a lot of the conspiracy narrative of BG1 except here it's also constantly questioning who you can really trust. The environments are beautiful looking and quite large, granting a lot of different paths to progress (usually).

However my praise ends there because there are so many issues. First is the actual stability of the game. CTD happens constantly, but seemingly for no rhyme or reason. Sometimes it will crash after 5 minutes, sometimes it will last a few hours. My GPU is not running hard and I'm not the only one who has been dealing with the same issue. Second is the terrible navigation of the maps themselves. The camera is really easy to bug out because you can't stray too far from your character and the maps have a lot of verticality to them. Characters are constantly failing to stick together when riding a platform up. Why not have the ability to select a formation and see exactly where they will stand (BG1 already figured this out ages ago). Tons of items are not highlighted by the alt key, you have to pixel hunt and clicking on items can be difficult. Even clicking on a character is delayed and unreliable. The inventory management is a tedious mess of menus.

Third: The game is rather difficult, but mostly because the "easy" methods require tons of knowledge of the process beforehand. A blind playthrough seems impossible even on the normal difficulty. The combat isn't a ton of number crunching like Pathfinder, but you really need to figure out builds beforehand and there's a heavy reliance on spells and abilities. It's pretty damn close to minmaxing and with only 4 party members and a lack of ability to change during certain story events, you absolutely need to either follow a guide or plan extensively beforehand. Sure yo…

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering technical bugs, including missing textures or unrendered buildings, enemies teleporting, or objects failing to load properly.

citations.review_text:
I can understand why the game has been so praised and hyped up. The writing is good, the environments are nice, and the soundtrack is great. However, I ran into so many gameplay and technical issues early on in the game that I almost completely lost the interest interest in playing. I've verified the game files, my computer is definitely good enough to run the game, and my friend says he hasn't had nearly as many issues, so I have no idea why it's been like this. Some of the main issues:

- Useless autosave system. A major portion of my playtime is just redoing hours of lost progress because I forgot to quicksave enough. Why couldn't they at least make it so that it autosaves after major conversations/events or after leveling up, for example?!

- Amount of bugs. I've encountered a weirdly high amount of bugs during my playthroughs. I've had to redo progress way too many times due to annoying things like enemies teleporting to where they shouldn't be, getting stuck out of bounds, visual or aural bugs, or some other annoying issues.

- Other issues include enemy vision going through terrain or solid objects when sneaking, being forced to stop sneaking and/or enter combat when you are in the vision cone of a non-hostile NPC that is not involved in combat in any way, and accidentally interacting with something while trying to just move your character. I really wish there was an option to change some interactions to use other buttons than the left mouse button.

- Misleading conversation options with irreversible outcomes. I've noticed that there are a lot of conversation options that seem completely neutral/non-hostile, but unexpectedly lead to the other party becoming hostile towards you. Even if you never attack them and only help them fight the other enemies, they will remain permanently hostile towards you, and there is no way to talk to them or pacify them. If you manage to knock them out with non-lethal attacks, the narrator says that they died, even though they d…

Game had me hooked until act 2 then it has been nothing but bugs and glitches. Things refuse to render in, buildings don't load the walls, I have verified files multiple times so at this point I have to think its the game. Hardware checks are fine so I have no idea why Balders gate hates my computer.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Players who reached the end of the adventure point out that later parts of the game feel less polished and detailed than the opening. There is also disappointment that character progression stops before the story ends, limiting end-game experimentation.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that parts of the second act and particularly the third act feel undercooked, less detailed, or less dynamic compared to the first act.

citations.review_text:
I could go on for hours about all the small things you can do in this game that affect other things down the line or the lovably tormented cast of characters or the great mod support or the insanely deep complexity of the gameplay if you allow yourself to sink into the details of it all, but I won't and will instead tell you to get this game. It's what other games should strive to be, in terms of sheer quality. 

One thing to note, though, is that parts of the second and especially the third act do feel a bit undercooked compared to the first, so perhaps go in with that expectation in mind. With how much there is to do, however, you might not even notice initially. Just that certain characters and plot threads don't seem as detailed or were given as much length as was needed to make them satisfying like others.

No words can describe my love for Baldur's Gate 3. It has gotten me through very hard times, with its incredible characters, narration, space for creative solutions and immersive world. I am 4 playthroughs in and I can't wait for my future ones. It has made me cry, laugh, think and more. Sharing this journey with people I love has been a pleasure. Seeing the work and passion that was put in every patch and update was great. Plus, the sheer amount of high quality mods for this game is insane!

Other than hoping for a future iteration where the city of Baldur's Gate is entirely explorable (Act 3 feels a bit rushed), my only complaint is that I just wish trans representation was better. Don't get me wrong, I am glad gaming as a whole has made the great strides it has, but as a nonbinary person I would have appreciated more androgynous and less "binary" character creation options, including voices. This is most likely a wider issue with D&D in general, but no one really discusses what being nonbinary or trans means to the various cultures, faiths, races and individual people of Faerun. I personally don't think being able to pick your genitals matters as much as the worldbuilding and RP possibilities that emerge for everyone from better trans visibility.

That said you can basically kill AI in the game, so 10/10
Nothing much to say, really. Game's pretty good, lots of choice. The only downside is act 3 that is too big and my completionist ass wanted to do everything, so it got boring after a while.

Spoiler free

Baldur's gate 3 was my first introduction to DnD, and it did not dissapoint at all! This is by far the biggest RPG I have ever played. It took me 190 hours to complete the game because there was so much to explore. The fighting system took me a while to get, but considering I was not familiar with the real tabletop counterpart, I think it was implemented really well. 
The characters are well-written. Their backstories are good, and freedom in the ways you can influence them is always welcome. Everyone has a chance for redemption. The amount of lines in this game is mindblowing! They really thought of everything: the character you play, choices you have made, your party and relationships. Everything. 
The soundtrack is perfect - memorable leitmotives, loud orchestra and beautiful vocals. 
My interest peaked in act 2, but dropped slightly in act 3 - it was less dynamic compared to previous ones. But the ending was very satisfying. In fact, the game as a whole is a masterpiece. You can just tell how much time and passion was poured into it. Even though I have completed it once, you can play it in so many different ways you will not get bored.
10/10, I recommend it to anyone.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that character progression halts upon reaching level 12, which feels premature given that the adventure is still ongoing.

citations.review_text:
Baldur's Gate 3 is easily one of the best RPGs I've ever played. From the moment you begin your adventure, it's clear just how much love and care Larian Studios poured into every corner of the game. The story is phenomenal, the world feels alive, and the lore behind each companion and major character is so rich that I found myself wanting to learn more about everyone I met. Every playthrough feels like it has something new to discover.

One of my favorite aspects is how the game respects the legacy of the Baldur's Gate series. Seeing beloved characters return from the previous games was an incredible experience, and it made the world feel like a true continuation rather than just another sequel. It's the kind of fan service that's earned and meaningful.

If I had one complaint, it's the level cap. Reaching level 12 feels like the adventure is still building toward even greater challenges, yet character progression comes to a halt. I would've loved to continue growing my character and experimenting with even more powerful abilities. Thankfully, the modding community has stepped in with incredible work that expands the experience beyond the base game.

I also want to give credit where it's due—not only to Larian Studios for creating such a masterpiece, but also to the talented mod creators who continue to breathe new life into the game. Their passion has made an already outstanding RPG even more replayable.

Overall, Baldur's Gate 3 is a masterpiece and a love letter to CRPG fans. Despite my wish for a higher level cap, it's a game I'll continue coming back to for years to come. Thank you, Larian Studios, and thank you to the amazing modding community for making this unforgettable adventure possible.

Given how hyped this game is, I would like to give you an in-depth analysis of both its positive and negative aspects and explain to you why I don’t recommend Baldur’s Gate 3 for most players. I will break this review down into the Good, the Bad and the Ugly:

The Good:
Let’s start with what makes this game truly shine.
Characters. You’ll get up to 10 recruitable companions with lots of unique dialogues and (for the most part) their own personal quests, some of which fantastically written, revealing rich origin stories including deep character development. Add stellar voice acting on top of all that and you get a highly immersive and memorable experience! 
Motion capture animations. Another reason why this game and its characters are so immersive is the motion capture animations. I think I’ve never experienced so many characters in a single video game coming so vividly and iconically to life as in bg3. Again, the voice acting adds massively to that.
Adjusting Dungeons & Dragons rules. For those of you who are unfamiliar with the original pen and paper game, it’s extremely unbalanced, especially when comparing the different classes to play. In the community, it’s widely known that there is a huge power gap between spellcaster and martial classes which gradually widens from middle to late levels. Larian studios apparently learned from DnD players homebrewing and elegantly solved this by cutting the maximum level down to 12 (which is btw how most tabletop DnD campaigns are being played) and redesigning certain classes.
Soundtrack. It’s all you could ask for in an RPG: epic during intense moments, soft during emotional moments, dreamy during exploration and overall fantastical.

The Bad:
As cool and amazing as the good stuff sounds, there is a lot of bad stuff we need to address here.
Tutorial is very lackluster for gamers with zero DnD experience. If you’re completely new to DnD, you should probably stop here because this game won’t even teach you the basics properly. …
